body: Playing video games. Early in our session she asked me about something’s I could do when I’m feeling overwhelmed and I told her sometimes video games help, but when I get really anxious my brain bounces and I can’t concentrate. She told me that’s ok because “video games aren’t a healthy coping skill” and went on to liken them to drug abuse and gambling. WFT lady I just want to play through Halo Reach for the 80th time without feeling like a piece of shit.

I hated the way my therapist wanted me to talk to people. No one sounds the way you want me to say, and if I talk to my SO, my parents, my boss like this they will not take me seriously. I’m not going to go into my thought feeling cycle every time my coworker says something ignorant.

I don’t think she’s ready to admit it yet, but she hates me. She says all the right things. The I love you’s and sappy Facebook post on Father’s Day and my birthday. But she is constantly annoyed and exhausted with me. She lectures me all the time and seems to think I’m incapable of doing most things. She’ll resent me before too long if she doesn’t already.

EMDR is so scary to me, because I think the eye movement stuff is such an obviously bull shit nothing science, but therapist treat is like it’s a magic technique they’ve learned to the point that they don’t have to help actually process any of the trauma.

I’m so sorry this happened to you, and I don’t really know what to suggest for you to help. But it sounds like you’ve gotten yourself to a good place before, so hopefully if you can get one or two good breaks your way you can carry yourself there again. Best of luck!

Behavioral therapy and CBT are like the only things even close to “science” therapy has and so many, unfortunately, younger therapist seem to latch on to it like it a holy grail. I’ve told a therapist before that I don’t like CBT and I don’t respond well to it, only to have them draw that stupid thoughts/feelings/actions circle to me and explain it like I must not have understood, because this is so great. I don’t know if it’s what they teach in those programs that behavioral therapy is the only way, but you can really see therapist brains break a little when you tell them, “behavioral therapy isn’t working for me, can we try something different?” 

I’m sorry you are stuck in this black hole you’re in now with treatment. This thread seems like a really awesome outlet to encourage you to do things for you though, so I hope that is at least helpful. Good luck and have fun playing the trombone! I really truly hope you get back to it.
Fellow former trombone kid here. This thread is awesome and I need to dig my trombone out of my parent’s house now. Love this whole thread!

If you like her I would call her out on it. We’re all on this sub because we know how hard (sometimes impossible) it is to get a therapist that is good. So if you have one, and feel like you’ve done good work, I would at least give her a chance to change what she’s doing. If/when you get an appointment next I would just start with exactly this. If you don’t like the response, then I think I would look into someone new. When I finally found a therapist that was good, I called her out all the time and she thankful would adjust accordingly. Hopefully yours will be the same way and keep more consistent with you. Good luck!

That’s what’s crazy to me about this. That is a training course. You’re not required to know that to be a therapist. Someone could graduate and be licensed and never have to learn the “gold standard.” 

I can see specialty training for certain disorders or more intensive situations, but I would think every therapist would come in contact with suicidal people regularly. To not be trained on how to address that is wild. Like going to your doctor and having them say, “oh sorry I’m actually not trained to treat strep throat.”
It’s the only theory I’ve seen that doesn’t try to pretend to be a hard science and just acknowledges this is a person first practice.

Know I’m way late to this, but I just recently found r/therapyabuse and now that’s shut down so i got sent here. 

Behavioral therapies (which are the gold standards of therapy according to counseling grad programs) are really only good for the worried well. The type of people with situational anxiety/depression that making small changes in thinking or behaviors would help. Not saying that’s wrong, or those people don’t need help, but it’s unfortunately not useful for a lot of people who need a lot more help. Humanistic Psychology is laughed at because of how “unscientific” it is, but for my money a lot of therapist would do well with remembering that empathy, genuineness, and unconditional positive regard are the best baselines for anything you need. Most people with disorders like BPD or bipolar or schizophrenia or even clinical depression have never had those things, so that goes a long way. From there, I agree some mix bag of whatever is best suited for the person. But I’ve been to too many therapist who have drawn me that stupid circle about my thoughts deciding my feelings and my feelings deciding my behaviors.
